SPACE CRAFT JOURNAL / PLANNING & LAYOUTS

Principles of interior design.

Build the plan around the working day. This Space Craft planning note looks at principles of interior design through the choices that affect everyday use, the details worth testing and the questions to take into your project brief.

Space Craft editorialPlanning note · 4 min read
IN THIS NOTEMap activity before assigning desksMake the routes legibleBalance density with choiceCombine daylight and task needsBefore you decide
01 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Map activity before assigning desks

Write down the tasks people perform, how often teams overlap and when visitors arrive. A desk count alone will not reveal the need for private calls, project tables or storage.

02 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Make the routes legible

Sketch the path from entry to reception, work areas, meeting settings and shared support. Test the layout with furniture drawn to scale, doors in use and accessible routes considered.

03 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Balance density with choice

Compare a focused-work setting with the busiest collaborative setting. Where they meet, think about sound, sightlines and transitions rather than using one open area for every task.

04 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Combine daylight and task needs

Look at window positions, screens and the time of day each space is used. Plan blinds or shading alongside electric lighting so that brightness and glare can be managed together.

BEFORE YOU DECIDE

Take this into your brief.

  • Record attendance patterns before fixing seat numbers.
  • Mark quiet work, conversations and visitor movement separately.
  • Test the layout with the people who will use it.

Write down one priority, one constraint and one question you still need to answer. Review them beside the plan or material sample before agreeing the next design decision.

General design considerations for discussion. Product suitability, technical performance, statutory requirements and project pricing need appropriate, project-specific review. Images are illustrative.
